_note: Single source of truth for the names we have given addresses in Lords2.exe.
GOG Windows build, 21 Jul 2009, 1,031,680 bytes, ImageBase 0x400000, no ASLR.
Adding a name is a one-line edit here. Then:
node tools/symbols/symbols_md.js            regenerate the tables in docs/symbols.md
node tools/symbols/symbols_md.js --check    fail if docs/symbols.md is out of date
analyzeHeadless ... -postScript ApplySymbols.java   push the names into Ghidra
confidence: 'verified' = read out of the binary or an exact invariant in the data.
'inferred'  = consistent with everything measured, not proven.
'signature' is optional; when present it is applied to the function in Ghidra and
its parameter names are what docs/symbols.md shows beside the name.
'comment' becomes the Ghidra plate comment (functions) or EOL comment (globals).

functions.name: Pl8_DrawFrame
functions.signature: undefined4 Pl8_DrawFrame(void * buf, int frame, int x, int y)
functions.comment: Reads the frame record at buf + frame*0x10 + 8, range-checks the data offset, calls the clipper, dispatches to a blitter. Independently confirms the 8-byte header / 16-byte record layout inferred from offset arithmetic. Also reads record bytes +12, +13 and +14.

functions.name: Clip_Horizontal
functions.comment: Computes horizontal clipping and sets g_clipState, g_clipVisibleWidth, g_clipSrcSkip, g_clipDstAdvance.

functions.name: Clip_Vertical
functions.comment: Sets g_blitRowCount to height - rowsClippedAtTop, unconditionally. That is why the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

functions.name: Blit_Unclipped
functions.comment: Copies g_spriteWidth bytes per row, skipping zero bytes; 4x unrolled. Loops g_blitRowCount rows - the clipped row count, not the frame height. Palette index 0 is transparent: this is an engine property, not something in the file format.

functions.name: Blit_ClippedLeft
functions.comment: Selected when g_clipState is 1.

functions.name: Blit_ClippedRight
functions.comment: As Blit_Unclipped, but also advances the source pointer by the clipped-off remainder each row.

functions.name: Glyph_Draw
functions.comment: Text blitter. Shifts the destination down by frame-record byte 0x0D before clipping, reserving rows above the rectangle. The only consumer of that byte.

functions.name: Eng_GroupBase
functions.comment: Returns the byte offset of an L2.eng group, read as the low 24 bits of the u32 at file offset 8 + group*4. See docs/formats/eng.md.

functions.name: Eng_DrawString
functions.signature: void Eng_DrawString(int group, int index, int x, int y, undefined * font, undefined4 colour)
functions.comment: Draws string `index` of L2.eng group `group`: Eng_GroupBase(group), then skip `index` NUL-terminated strings, then skip any bytes below 0x20. The (group, index) pairs in the callers are the best evidence available for what a subsystem is.

functions.name: File_ReadChunk
functions.signature: int File_ReadChunk(char * name, void * buf, uint len, long offset)
functions.comment: open / lseek / read / close. Retries twice after chdir on failure - almost certainly the original CD-path lookup.

functions.name: Restore_WorkingDir
functions.comment: chdir back, reporting via getcwd on failure.

functions.name: Armoury_LoadScreen
functions.comment: A worked example of the load-then-draw path: selects a weapon sprite set from a global, reads it into a 250 KB buffer, then calls Pl8_DrawFrame.

functions.name: Map_InitScenario
functions.comment: Whole map bring-up for scenario g_scenarioIndex: Map_LoadPlanes, Map_LoadLattice, Map_LoadTileSets, Map_PlaceDwellings, then Merchant_PickStartCounties.

functions.name: Map_LoadPlanes
functions.comment: Reads the six 64x64 byte planes of a map slot, at slot offsets +0x0000 ... +0x5000, in a 64x64 nest (y outer, x inner). Tracks the highest county id below 0x11 into g_countyCount, and dispatches plane 4 to Merchant_RouteAppend (castle tiles) or PlayerStart_Record (settlement tiles). See docs/formats/maps.md.

functions.name: Map_LoadLattice
functions.comment: Reads the trailing 65x129 layer - for(row < 0x81) for(col < 0x41) - storing byte + 0x0FFF0000 into a dword array of row stride 0x104.

functions.name: Map_LoadTileSets
functions.comment: Selects MAPnn.PL8 from a 16-byte name table indexed by scenario >> 2, and one of four variants per file (the seasons) by scenario & 3.

functions.name: Map_PlaceDwellings
functions.comment: Sweeps the 64x64 grid and, for each tile with a county in 1..17 and plane0 bit 0x20 set, increments a per-county counter and rewrites the tile's graphic index to Roads frame 80, 84 or 104 - the three crop states. maps-layers.md 2.4 reads bit 0x20 as farmland on this evidence.

functions.name: Map_RenderIso
functions.comment: Walks the 65x129 lattice. Cells below 0x0FFF0000 hold a runtime offset into the tile array; cells still holding 0x0FFF0000 + b are off-map surround, where b is the background tile graphic index from the file.

functions.name: Map_DrawTile
functions.signature: uint Map_DrawTile(undefined4 x, undefined4 y, int tileOffset)
functions.comment: Draws one map tile. bank = tile[+2] & 0x1c selects one of five sprite tables; tile[+3] is the frame index within it; tile[+1] is the flags and tile[+7] the county.

functions.name: Map_LatticeCellForTile
functions.comment: Reverse lookup: scans the screen lattice for a given tile-array offset to find its screen cell.

functions.name: Unit_Spawn
functions.signature: undefined4 Unit_Spawn(byte type, int x, int y, byte owner)
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the 150-entry unit array g_units (stride 0x1A4) and places it at tile (x, y). Requires the tile to hold no unit and to have plane-0 bits 0xFC clear. Writes the unit index into byte +5 of the runtime tile record and sets bit 0x01 of byte +2. Types seen: 1 = army, 2 = revolting peasants, 3 = merchant, 4 = transport.

functions.name: Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear(int x, int y, int r)
functions.comment: Scans the (2r+1)^2 box around (x, y), clipped to the map, for a tile with no unit on it and plane-0 bit 0x01 (road) set. Returns 1 and leaves the tile in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY.

functions.name: Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear(int x, int y, int r)
functions.comment: As Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear but accepts plane0 & 0xFD == 0 - plain grass, with or without the county-boundary bit. The fallback when no free road tile exists.

functions.name: County_FindFreeRoadTile
functions.comment: Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear around the county's anchor tile for r = 1, 2, 3.

functions.name: County_FindFreeOpenTile
functions.comment: Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear around the county's anchor tile for r = 1, 2, 3.

functions.name: Merchant_RouteAppend
functions.comment: Appends `county` to the first free cell of row `route - 1` of g_merchantRoutes. Called from Map_LoadPlanes for every castle tile with a non-zero plane 4. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

functions.name: Merchant_ResetRoutes
functions.comment: Zeroes the 6x16 g_merchantRoutes table and the 6-byte g_merchantStartCounty array, at the top of Map_LoadPlanes.

functions.name: Merchant_PickStartCounties
functions.comment: For each of the six routes, picks a start county no earlier route has claimed: entry 0, then entries 2, 4, 6..., then 3, 5, 7... after running off the end; entry 1 is never tried and it gives up after five retries. Because g_merchantStartCounty starts zeroed, a row with no free candidate stores 0 - which stops Merchant_SpawnAll dead. On slot 15 (Rorschach) the dedup fails and two merchants share county 8.

functions.name: Merchant_StartCountyTaken
functions.comment: 1 if `county` already appears in g_merchantStartCounty. Note it also returns 1 for county 0, because unset entries are 0.

functions.name: Merchant_SpawnAll
functions.comment: Spawns one type-3 merchant, owner 6 (nobody), on a free road tile near each start county, stopping at the first zero start county. Sets the unit's route index (its name, L2.eng group 5) and route cursor, and counts them into g_merchantCount. 18 of the 44 shipped maps get all six merchants; one gets a single merchant.

functions.name: Merchant_AdvanceAll
functions.comment: Turn phase 6, step 1. For every type-3 unit awaiting a destination, walks row (unitIndex - 1) of g_merchantRoutes cyclically from the unit's route cursor, skipping entries above g_countyCount, and sends the merchant to the next county on its route. It indexes the table by unit index, not by the unit's stored route number - which only works because the merchants occupy unit slots 1..6.

functions.name: PlayerStart_Record
functions.comment: Writes {county, slot} into g_playerStartTable[slot] and counts non-zero slots into g_playerStartCount. Called from Map_LoadPlanes for settlement tiles with a non-zero plane 4: the player start table. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

functions.name: UnitPanel_Draw
functions.comment: Draws the info panel for the selected unit. Its Eng_DrawString (group, index) pairs name every unit type: L2.eng group 31 strings 0 'Merchant.', 5 'Revolting peasants.', 2 'Supplies for', 15/16 army; descriptions 12/13/14/15/16. For a merchant it also draws group 5 indexed by the route number - the merchant's name.

functions.name: Transport_Deliver
functions.comment: If the type-4 unit's destination county matches, adds its cargo to that county's stores.

functions.name: Transport_Spawn
functions.signature: void Transport_Spawn(int owner, int county, byte dest)
functions.comment: Creates a type-4 transport near `county` and deducts the cargo from that county's stores.

functions.name: Unit_EnterOccupiedTile
functions.comment: Resolves what happens when the moving unit enters a tile already holding one. Returns immediately for types 3 and 4, so merchants and transports are never attacked; an enemy transport is captured instead.

functions.name: Unit_TrampleTile
functions.comment: Damages a crop tile an army passes through in a county it does not own. Begins `if (type != 3 && type != 4)` - merchants and transports do no damage.

functions.name: Unit_BurnDwelling
functions.comment: Burns a dwelling an army passes through in a county it does not own, and cuts that county's population. Same type-3/type-4 exemption.

functions.name: Battle_Start
functions.comment: Brings a battle up: builds the battlefield (Battlefield_BuildRandom, Battlefield_BuildFromSkr or Battlefield_BuildCastle), then Battle_InitArmies, then the first unit/figure update passes. See docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Battle_InitArmies
functions.comment: Chooses the battlefield size class from the two armies, clears the figure and unit arrays, then raises both sides. Also computes each side's autocalc strength as sum(count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t]) over troop types 0..6.

functions.name: Battle_RaiseSide
functions.signature: void Battle_RaiseSide(int armyUnit, int outnumbered, int side)
functions.comment: Turns one army record into battle units. Walks the 11 troop types in g_raiseOrder, and for each splits the men into units of at most maxFigures*g_menPerFigure. Siege counts are multiplied by g_menPerFigure so that one engine is one figure. `side` is 4 or 0.

functions.name: Battle_RaiseSideSiege
functions.signature: void Battle_RaiseSideSiege(int armyUnit, int outnumbered, int side)
functions.comment: The castle-defender variant of Battle_RaiseSide: uses g_raiseOrderSiege (8 troop types, no catapult/tower/ram), forces archers and crossbowmen to at most 3 figures per unit, and places units by wall slot rather than by deployment marker.

functions.name: BattleUnit_LoadTroopStats
functions.comment: Copies one row of g_troopBattleStats (0x004D96D0, stride 0x14) into scratch globals, then the matching row of g_missileStats (0x004D97B0) selected by the weapon class in field +0x0C.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Create
functions.signature: void BattleUnit_Create(int siegePlacement, int troopType, int outnumbered, int side, int men, int owner, int mercenary)
functions.comment: Allocates a battle unit and fills it with ceil(men / g_menPerFigure) figures laid out in a rectangle. Sets the unit category from the troop type, and copies the troop and missile stats into every figure.

functions.name: BattleMan_Create
functions.signature: undefined4 BattleMan_Create(byte troopType, int x0, int dx, int y0, int dy, int owner, short unit)
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the 80-entry figure array g_battleMen (stride 0x1B0), places it on the battlefield, writes its index into cell byte +5 and links it to its unit. Returns 0 when all 80 slots are in use, which silently truncates the army.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Alloc
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the 80-entry unit array g_battleUnits (stride 0x34); a slot is free when byte +0 (owner) is zero. Leaves the index in g_lastBattleUnit.

functions.name: Missile_Spawn
functions.signature: undefined4 Missile_Spawn(byte owner, int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Allocates one of the 100 slots of g_missiles (stride 0x4C) and sets its start and target positions in 1/32-cell units. Used for arrows, bolts, catapult shot, thrown oil, fire and falling figures.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Clear
functions.comment: Zeroes one 0x34-byte battle unit record.

functions.name: BattleMan_Clear
functions.comment: Zeroes one 0x1B0-byte battle figure record.

functions.name: BattleMen_ClearAll
functions.comment: Zeroes g_battleMen[1..80]. The loop bound 0x51 is what fixes the figure count at 80.

functions.name: BattleUnits_ClearAll
functions.comment: Zeroes g_battleUnits[1..80].

functions.name: BattleMan_Destroy
functions.comment: Clears the figure off its battlefield cell and zeroes its record.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateAllMen
functions.comment: Per-frame sweep over g_battleMen[1..80]. Applies burning damage on surface 10/17, ages the figure, then dispatches g_troopTickTable[troopType] - which reloads the per-troop stats and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state].

functions.name: Battle_UpdateAllUnits
functions.comment: Per-frame sweep over g_battleUnits[1..80]. Recentres each unit on its figures, and runs its order handler unless byte +1 (human controlled) is set. Three dispatch tables: field, siege attacker, siege defender. Counts field +0x14 down from 500 and re-targets at zero.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateMissiles
functions.comment: Rebuilds the cell -> figure occupancy map for all 80 figures, then steps every missile.

functions.name: Missile_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Steps g_missiles[1..100].

functions.name: Missile_Step
functions.comment: Advances the current missile by its steps-per-tick and, when it enters a cell holding an enemy figure, applies the missile damage formula: elevation scaling, minus the target armour, minus the crossbow-vs-engine reduction, floor 2, accumulated into the target hits pool; every 100 hits kills one man. See docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Melee_Tick
functions.comment: One tick of a melee duel. The attacker decrements the defender recovery counter; when it expires the defender takes the attacker melee attack value into its hits pool, and once per exchange the attacker heavy-blow bonus as well. 100 hits kills one man; the attacker role swaps when the exchange counter runs out.

functions.name: BattleMan_BurnTick
functions.comment: Adds 3/6/9/12 hits per tick (1/3/5/7 for siege engines) by battlefield size class to a figure standing on a burning cell, +1/+2 more if the owner is human-controlled. Threshold 100 (160 for engines) kills one man.

functions.name: BattleMan_RecomputeStrength
functions.comment: Sets the figure strength band 0..3 by comparing its remaining men against g_strengthBand1/2/3 (75%, 50%, ~19-25% of a full figure), then loads its melee attack value from g_meleeAttackTable[troopType][band].

functions.name: Battle_LoadStrengthBands
functions.comment: Loads the three strength-band thresholds for the current battlefield size class from g_strengthBandTable.

functions.name: BattleMan_FireMissile
functions.comment: Missile reload and fire. Acquires a target 10 ticks before the reload interval expires, then spawns a missile whose power is the figure missile damage scaled by its strength band (full, 4/5, 3/4, 1/2).

functions.name: BattleMan_StateIdle
functions.comment: Figure state 5. Advances the animation, and fires if the figure has a missile weapon.

functions.name: BattleMan_LookForMelee
functions.comment: Figure state 7. If an adjacent enemy exists, locks both figures into state 4 facing each other, one as attacker and one as defender; otherwise falls back to idle or missile search.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateMelee
functions.comment: Figure state 4. Drops out if the opponent is gone or dead, otherwise runs Melee_Tick.

functions.name: Melee_FindAdjacentEnemy
functions.comment: Tests the eight neighbouring cells in the order N, NW, NE, W, E, SW, SE, S and returns the direction of the first live enemy figure, or 8. Siege engines (troop types 7..10) are never returned.

functions.name: Missile_FindTarget
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTarget(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Nearest live enemy figure within `range` by Manhattan distance, capped at 160. The unit ordered target is forced to distance 0; siege-engine targets get a +35 distance penalty.

functions.name: Melee_ResetExchange
functions.comment: Sets how long this figure holds the attacking role in a duel, from its animation class: 0, 40, 80, 80 or 120 ticks.

functions.name: Melee_ResetRecovery
functions.comment: Adds the figure recovery interval (+0x18B) to its recovery counter. That interval is the rate at which the figure can be hit in melee, so it is the real melee defence: peasants and archers 6 ticks, crossbowmen 8, macemen and swordsmen 12, knights 16, pikemen 30.

functions.name: BattleMan_Step
functions.comment: Movement. Waits g_troopBattleStats[type].moveDelay ticks per sub-step, accumulates 2 per step until 17, then takes the next path direction and calls BattleMan_TryStepDir. Knights have delay 0 and pikemen 4, which is why knights are fastest and pikemen slowest.

functions.name: BattleMan_TryStepDir
functions.comment: Turns a direction 0..7 into a neighbouring cell offset, clamps at the map edge and calls Cell_TryEnter.

functions.name: Cell_TryEnter
functions.comment: Decides whether a figure may enter a battlefield cell: 1 free, 0 blocked by a friendly figure or flag 0x40, 2 impassable (flags 0x10/0x80, or an elevation change of more than 1), 5 flag 0x20 for a non-zero side, 999 enemy figure present.

functions.name: Melee_AdjacentEnemyDir
functions.signature: int Melee_AdjacentEnemyDir(int x, int y, int cellOffset)
functions.comment: Scans the eight neighbours via g_cellNeighbourOffsets and returns the direction of an enemy figure standing at the same elevation, or 8.

functions.name: Dir_FromDelta
functions.signature: undefined4 Dir_FromDelta(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Eight-way direction from (x,y) to (tx,ty): 0 N, 1 NE, 2 E, 3 SE, 4 S, 5 SW, 6 W, 7 NW, 8 same cell. This is the encoding of the figure facing byte.

functions.name: Dist_Manhattan
functions.signature: int Dist_Manhattan(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns |dx| + |dy| and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy.

functions.name: Dist_Chebyshev
functions.signature: int Dist_Chebyshev(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns max(|dx|, |dy|) and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy.

functions.name: Table_Lookup
functions.signature: int Table_Lookup(int x, int * pairs, int count, int dflt)
functions.comment: Generic (threshold, value) ladder: returns the value of the first pair whose threshold exceeds x, else the default. Used for the battlefield size class and the men-per-figure scale.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildFromSkr
functions.comment: Loads one 80x80 .skr terrain layer and expands it into the 8-byte-per-cell battlefield, including bridge parts and the two 12-slot deployment marker arrays. See docs/formats/skr.md.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildRandom
functions.comment: The open-field battlefield generator: writes the same cell array and the same deployment slot arrays as Battlefield_BuildFromSkr, but from the campaign map rather than a .skr layer.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildCastle
functions.comment: The siege battlefield builder; the third writer of the cell array.

functions.name: Skr_ReadMap
functions.comment: Reads one .skr terrain layer: 0x1900 bytes at file offset index * 0x1900 + 0x1674. See docs/formats/skr.md.

functions.name: Deploy_SlotForUnit
functions.comment: Picks a deployment cell for the n-th unit of a side from the 12-slot marker array: side 0 uses the 0x04 marker slots at 0x00553150, side 4 the 0x0F marker slots at 0x005531B0. There are only 12 slots, so a side with more than 12 units reads past the end.

functions.name: Deploy_SlotForUnitSiege
functions.comment: The castle-defender placement: maps the troop type to one of the marker slots rather than using the unit ordinal, with a rotating fallback list.

functions.name: Formation_OffsetX
functions.signature: int Formation_OffsetX(int footprint, int rows, int i)
functions.comment: Column offset of figure i in a units rectangle: (i / rows) * footprint.

functions.name: Formation_OffsetY
functions.signature: int Formation_OffsetY(int footprint, int rows, uint i, int side)
functions.comment: Row offset of figure i: (i % rows) * footprint, negated for side 0 so both sides face each other.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Recentre
functions.comment: Sets the unit position to the centre of the bounding box of its live figures.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Order
functions.signature: void BattleUnit_Order(int unit, int x, int y, int attackTarget, int fromPlayer, int facing)
functions.comment: Gives a battle unit a destination. Missile units stop short of the target by (range/8 - 3) cells; a unit that mixes missile and melee figures is split into two units.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Classify
functions.comment: Recomputes the unit category from the troop types it still contains: catapult 5, tower 6, ram 7, oil 8, any missile figure 1, otherwise 3. The category selects the order handler.

functions.name: BattleDebug_Panel
functions.comment: The developers' own battle debug overlay. It prints figure and unit fields beside their original labels - FIGURE / map x / map y / tg x / tg y / routed / hold it / state / on route / hits / walking / barred / target / dirc / delay / dly state / targeted / selected / selctd seen / polar dirc / mov straff, and GROUP / re targ / map x / map y / targ x / targ y / orders / firing. This is the primary evidence for the field names in docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Troops_Load
functions.comment: Parses TROOPS.ENG / TROOPS2.ENG / TROOPS3.ENG into g_troopsTable. The in-memory layout is short[35][2][5][11] - side outer (stride 0x6E), difficulty inner (stride 0x16) - and difficulty groups 0,1,3,4 are then overwritten with Normal at +16%, +8%, -8% and -16% on troop types 0..6 only.

functions.name: Skirmish_FillArmies
functions.comment: Copies one row of g_troopsTable into the two army records used by the battle, choosing the side by whether the player is the attacker and the difficulty column per player, then recomputes each army total men (+0x168) and autocalc strength.

functions.name: Skirmish_Setup
functions.comment: Sets up a stand-alone skirmish: army records 1 and 2, loads BATTLES.ENG and the TROOPS table, fills both armies.

functions.name: BattleMen_SwapPlaces
functions.comment: When a figure walks into a friendly figure of the same troop type it swaps places with it, carrying position, cell, hits and men across. Returns 2 on a swap.

functions.name: Order_StopShortOfTarget
functions.signature: void Order_StopShortOfTarget(int x, int y, int tx, int ty, int range)
functions.comment: Pulls a move destination back so the unit halts (range - 3) cells from its target, leaving the result in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. This is how missile units stop at firing range instead of closing.

functions.name: Path_Search
functions.signature: void Path_Search(int mode, int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The battlefield pathfinder. A uniform-cost breadth-first flood fill over the 80x80 grid with a circular queue: g_pathCost[cell] holds cost+1 from the start, a cell is expanded only after being reached g_pathStepCost[cell] times (that is how terrain cost is charged), and a step is only allowed between cells whose elevation differs by at most 1. Skipped entirely when the target is adjacent or the straight line is clear.

functions.name: Path_SearchSiege
functions.signature: void Path_SearchSiege(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The variant of Path_Search used by figures in state 9 - the siege/wall path.

functions.name: Path_Extract
functions.signature: int Path_Extract(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Walks the g_pathCost field downhill from the destination back to the start, writing the route into g_pathWaypoints as (x,y) byte pairs and returning its length. Ties are broken towards the straight-line direction. Returns 0 for no path and 150 for adjacent or over-long.

functions.name: BattleMan_SetPath
functions.comment: Copies `length` waypoints out of g_pathWaypoints into the figure own list at +0x38, sets the count at +0x36 and marks the figure "on route".

functions.name: BattleMan_NextPathDir
functions.comment: Returns the direction towards the figure current waypoint and consumes it. The list is walked from the end, because Path_Extract builds it backwards from the destination.

functions.name: Dest_FindReachableNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Dest_FindReachableNear(int fromX, int fromY, int x, int y, int unit)
functions.comment: Expanding-ring search of radius 0..19 around (x,y) for a cell with the same surface type and elevation as the source, leaving it in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Used to fix up a move order that lands on unreachable ground.

functions.name: Path_LineIsClear
functions.signature: bool Path_LineIsClear(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Straight-line passability test; when it succeeds Path_Search does no work at all and the figure walks directly at its target.

functions.name: Path_BuildBlockedMap
functions.comment: Refreshes the per-cell blocking map the flood fill reads, from the live figure positions.

functions.name: BattleUnit_OrderToEnemyEnd
functions.comment: Sends the current unit to a slot of the opposing sides deployment marker - side 0 to the 0x0F marker, side 4 to the 0x04 marker. Together with Deploy_SlotForUnit this establishes that side 0 deploys at the 0x04 marker and side 4 at the 0x0F marker.

functions.name: Turn_Tick
functions.comment: Per-frame dispatcher on g_turnPhase (1..7). Phase 1 neutral-county upkeep, 2 army movement, 3 supply transports, 4 the players' turn, 5 peasant mobs, 6 merchants, 7 end of season. Increments g_turnPhaseStep every call.

functions.name: Turn_AdvancePhase
functions.comment: g_turnPhase++, wrapping 7 -> 1 (and then calling FUN_0049B6D3); resets g_turnPhaseStep and sets the next-phase preview at 0x0053F678.

functions.name: Turn_AllRealmsDone
functions.comment: Returns non-zero once every in-play realm's AI step counter (realm +0x00) has reached 999. The exit condition of phase 4.

functions.name: AI_RunTurnStep
functions.comment: One step of one realm's turn, round-robin over realms 1..5 through 0x0057C944. Realm +0x00 is a 1..14 program counter into fourteen sub-handlers; at 15 + 2*realm the realm is marked done (999). Skipped entirely when realm +0x05 (human) is set.

functions.name: Season_Advance
functions.comment: The end-of-season pipeline. Rolls g_seasonPrev/g_season/g_seasonNext and the year (when the season that ended was 4 = Winter), bumps g_turnCount, then calls 28 subsystem passes in a fixed order. This is the whole kingdom economy for one turn.

functions.name: Game_NewGame
functions.comment: New-game setup: year 1267/1268, g_season = 3, g_seasonNext = 4, then Map_InitScenario, Merchant_SpawnAll and one immediate Season_Advance - which is why a new game begins in Winter 1268.

functions.name: Rules_InitConstants
functions.comment: Writes the tunable economy scalars into .data at startup: g_grainYieldPerSack = 12, g_grainMaxSacksPerField = 10, g_foodPerHead = 10, g_foodPerSack = 6, g_dairyPerHead = 5, g_grainLabourDivisorAdv = 5, g_grainLabourDivisor = 2.

functions.name: Tax_CollectAll
functions.comment: Per county: rate = 320 + castle bonus (480/560/640/720/800 for castle types 1..5, i.e. +50/75/100/125/150%); take = Pct(Pct(population, rate), taxRate); credited to the owner realm's gold. Also writes the tax happiness delta 5 - taxRate + realm[+0x28] into county +0x0E.

functions.name: Tax_SumEmpireHappiness
functions.comment: realm[+0x28] = sum over the realm's counties of county +0x16 - the "Other counties" term of the tax happiness effect (L2.eng group 86 index 4). Sums signed bytes into a signed byte, so a large empire can overflow.

functions.name: Happiness_UpdateAll
functions.comment: happiness(+0x0C) = last(+0x0D) + tax(+0x0E) + health(+0x10) + ration(+0x11), copied to the display fields +0x12..+0x14, clamped 0..100, accumulated into +0x1C and averaged into +0x18. Unowned counties below 75 get a flat +5 recorded as "From events".

functions.name: Health_UpdateAll
functions.comment: health meter (+0x0B) += g_healthDeltaTable[rationLevel][healthBand], clamped 0..100; band (+0x09) = Table_Lookup(meter, g_healthBandLadder); happiness contribution (+0x10) = g_healthHappiness[band].

functions.name: Population_UpdateAll
functions.comment: births = Pct(pop, Pct(g_birthRateLadder(pop), happinessFactor)); deaths = Pct(pop, g_deathRateByHealth[band] + g_deathRateBySeason[season]); pop += births - deaths - emigrants + immigrants. Reproduces the shipped lastturn.sav exactly.

functions.name: Migration_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Emigration to the happiest adjacent county: pct = Pct(dHappiness, (100 - happiness)/3), movers = min(100, Pct(pop, pct)), halved for unowned counties. Fills county +0x3C/+0x40/+0x58 and the 16-byte source list at +0x48.

functions.name: Unrest_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Counts county +0x20 up while happiness is low and down while it recovers; at 4 it calls FUN_004AC185, which raises the revolting-peasant army. Human-owned counties get warning messages 0x96..0x99 as the counter climbs.

functions.name: Weather_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Dryness (+0x21D) += seasonal delta (Spring +8, Summer +24, Autumn +12, Winter -12) minus rand/8, doubled for one random county and half again for its neighbours; banded into +0x21B: <5 Flooding, <20 Storms, <70 Cloudy, <95 Sunny, else Drought, with Drought becoming Frost in Winter and Spring. Forced to Cloudy when Advanced Farming is off.

functions.name: Fertility_Update
functions.comment: county +0x208 += 6 * fallowFields(+0x1FF) - 3 * grainFields(+0x201), clamped to -100..100, forced to 0 when Advanced Farming is off. One fallow field per two grain fields is exactly break-even; cattle fields do not enter it.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimTick
functions.comment: Advances the 20 per-county field-progress words at +0x90 towards 800, at most 200 per season - the manual's "never more than a quarter of a field in a single season". Rewrites the tile graphic at each quarter.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimEstimate
functions.comment: The same walk without committing: fills +0xE4 (work remaining) and +0x214 (seasons to the next completed field) for the county panel.

functions.name: Grain_SeasonTick
functions.comment: The grain cycle. Entering Spring it sows (Grain_Sow, store -= seed); entering Summer and Autumn it grows; entering Winter it harvests into the store. Weather scales each stage. Also applies the rats/surplus random-event modifier at +0x1FC.

functions.name: Grain_Sow
functions.signature: int Grain_Sow(int county, int labour, int grainStore)
functions.comment: Largest sacksPerField in 10..1 such that grainFields*sacks fits both the grain store and the available labour (g_grainYieldPerSack * sown / labourDivisor). Sets county +0x1A7 when it had to fall back to a single field.

functions.name: Grain_Grow
functions.signature: int Grain_Grow(int county, int labour, int crop)
functions.comment: Mid-season crop step, entering Summer and Autumn.

functions.name: Grain_Harvest
functions.signature: int Grain_Harvest(int county, int labour, int crop)
functions.comment: Harvest step, entering Winter.

functions.name: Herd_SeasonTick
functions.comment: Herd (+0x250) growth: births/deaths from FUN_0044DA99, plus Pct(herd, g_herdWeatherPct[weather]) and the disease/wolves random-event modifier at +0x1FD.

functions.name: Ration_Apply
functions.comment: Picks the highest affordable ration level 0..5 (None/Quarter/Half/Normal/Double/Triple) by descending from the wanted level, requirement = DivCeil(pop, g_rationTable[l].div) * g_rationTable[l].mul plus garrisons when Armies Eat is on; spends dairy first, then splits the rest between livestock and grain by county +0x15F; writes the ration happiness delta 3*level - 8 to +0x11.

functions.name: Food_FromDairy
functions.comment: herd * g_dairyPerHead (5). The standing herd feeds five people per head per season without being slaughtered.

functions.name: Food_HeadsForPeople
functions.comment: DivCeil(people, g_foodPerHead) - one slaughtered animal feeds ten people.

functions.name: Food_SacksForPeople
functions.comment: DivCeil(people, g_foodPerSack) - one sack of grain feeds six people.

functions.name: Food_Available
functions.comment: herd*5 + slaughterable*10 + grain*6, the county's total feeding capacity this season.

functions.name: Industry_Produce
functions.signature: void Industry_Produce(int county, int commodity, int job, int baseEfficiency, int divisor)
functions.comment: One industry pass. output = min(resourceLimit, Pct(workers / divisor, efficiency)); commodity 0 wood (job 7, divisor 1, base efficiency 20), 1 iron (job 5, divisor 1, 15), 2 weapons (job 8, divisor 4, 15), 3 stone (job 6, divisor 2, 15). Weapons debit g_weaponCost from the realm's wood and iron.

functions.name: Castle_BuildTick
functions.comment: Advances castle construction in every county, promoting the castle type and raising its free garrison when the work reaches 100%.

functions.name: Castle_BuildEstimate
functions.comment: Fills the castle panel: work left (+0xF0) and seasons remaining (+0x1A6) from the outstanding work and the labour assigned.

functions.name: Wages_PayAll
functions.comment: realm[+0xFC] = Wages_ForRealm; if the treasury cannot cover it the realm goes through a five-stage bankruptcy escalation (messages 0xA0/0x10E, 0x11F, 0x10F, then FUN_004AD316) counted in realm +0x158.

functions.name: Wages_ForRealm
functions.comment: Sum of Wages_ForUnit over the realm's armies (unit type 1).

functions.name: Wages_ForUnit
functions.comment: men(+0x168) / 4 for a human owner; for an AI owner /3, /5, /10, /10 by difficulty. Matches the player-measured 250 men -> 62 crowns and 254 -> 63.

functions.name: Event_RollAll
functions.comment: Draws a random-event id from g_eventTable for each human-owned county after year 1268 and dispatches one of 24 handlers (0x87..0x8E, 0x12E..0x13D) that write the modifiers at county +0x1FB..+0x1FD or move happiness/health directly.

functions.name: AI_SetTaxRates
functions.comment: Sets county +0xB9 from happiness on one of four ladders (neutral counties, then three by AI personality), and grants the AI its per-turn difficulty bonus: gold from g_aiGoldGrant, plus free population, herd and grain scaled by difficulty.

functions.name: AI_ManageFields
functions.comment: For each of the realm's counties: start reclaiming when the field count is low for the population, then run one of two field-allocation strategies and Ration_Apply.

functions.name: Score_RankRealms
functions.comment: Recomputes each realm's score at +0x50 from counties, population, castles, armies and treasury, bubble-sorts realms 1..5 into the ranking table at 0x00565410 and writes the rank back to realm +0x2B.

functions.name: Save_Write
functions.comment: Writes every block listed in g_saveBlocks back to back, then appends the sixteen 12,800-byte castle plans from castles.dat. 267,028 + 16*12,800 = 471,828, the exact size of lastturn.sav.

functions.name: Save_RotateAndWrite
functions.comment: Rotates safeturn.sav <- old_turn.sav <- lastturn.sav and then calls Save_Write. Called from Game_NewGame and at each turn boundary.

functions.name: Castles_CreateFile
functions.comment: Creates castles.dat as sixteen zeroed 0x3200-byte blocks, one castle plan per county slot.

functions.name: Sync_CompareState
functions.comment: Multiplayer desync detector: walks three of the g_syncBlocks descriptors and reports the first record and byte that differ between the two state snapshots.

functions.name: Sync_Checksum
functions.comment: Sums the same descriptor-selected bytes into a per-frame checksum for the network layer.

functions.name: Panel_Happiness
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 85 ("Happiness in / Last season / From taxes / From ration / From health / From army / From ale / This Season / Average happiness / From events") next to county fields +0x0D, +0x12, +0x13, +0x14, +0x15, +0x194, +0x17, +0x0C and +0x18. This is what names those fields.

functions.name: Panel_Population
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 73 next to county +0x28 (last season), +0x30 (births), +0x34 (deaths), +0x38 (army), +0x3C/+0x58 (emigrants to), +0x40 (immigrants) and +0x24 (this season).

functions.name: Panel_Tax
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 86: "Tax rate" = county +0xB9, "People pay" = +0xC0, "This county" = realm +0x28 + county +0x0F, "Other counties" = county +0x16.

functions.name: Pct
functions.comment: x * p / 100. The whole economy is written in this.

functions.name: PctOf
functions.comment: a * 100 / b, 0 when b is 0.

functions.name: DivCeil
functions.comment: (a + b - 1) / b, 0 when b is 0.

functions.name: UnitOrder_None
functions.comment: The empty order handler: an immediate return. Seven of the 25 dispatch-table slots point at it - field category 0, siege-attacker 0 and 8, siege-defender 0, 5, 6 and 7 - so a unit of one of those categories never acts on its own. See docs/battle-ai.md.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage
functions.comment: Recomputed every 101 frames from Battle_UpdateAllUnits. Sums surviving men over all live figures, weighted 1/2/3/3/2/2/4 by troop type 0..6 and 1 for siege engines, split by figure byte +0x13 (owner is human). Leaves (aiMen * 100 / humanMen) - 100 in g_aiStrengthAdvantage, plus a -10..+21 jitter when g_deterministicBattle is zero. Every order handler branches on that one number.

functions.name: BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures
functions.comment: Runs while g_battlePhase == 2. Rebuilds every unit's owner, figure count and first/last figure index from the live figure array; ages the unit timers +0x0C (recently hit), +0x0E (order lock), +0x0F (firing) and +0x2D; sets +0x0D when any figure is in melee and +0x11 when any is on the wall; and, when a figure raises its was-hit flag +0x15, records the attacking figure's unit in +0x0A and sets +0x0C to 50. It runs once per frame from Battle_Frame, so that grudge lasts 50 frames against a 200-frame think interval. This is where the AI's memory of who is hitting it comes from.

functions.name: BattleUnit_JoinMelee
functions.comment: Called from BattleMan_Step on both units the moment a figure walks into an enemy. Puts every other live, non-melee figure of the unit into state 8 (free pursuit). Skipped for human-controlled units, for missile units (category 1) and while the unit's order lock +0x0E is non-zero - so an AI melee unit piles in on contact and a player's unit does not.

functions.name: Battle_CountMenByType
functions.comment: Census of surviving men. Among figures whose owner is not human it totals all men into g_aiMenTotal, crossbowmen plus archers into g_aiMenMissile and knights into g_aiMenKnight; it also totals each army's men separately. The field and siege handlers read those three to decide when their side has run out of a troop class.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldMissile
functions.comment: Field battle, unit category 1 (archers, crossbowmen). Thinks once per 200 frames and not at all while any of its figures is in melee. Above the aggression threshold it shoots the nearest enemy unit if it was hit in the last 50 frames, otherwise advances halfway, holds, and advances again on an `orders` schedule. Below it, it shoots its attacker, answers a rally request, or sits on rally waypoint 0 every fourth think - and once it has been hit more than ten times it backs two cells away from its attacker.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldFoot
functions.comment: Field battle, unit category 2 (peasants, pikemen). Above the aggression threshold it marches to the enemy end of the field for ten thinks then charges. Below it, being attacked either raises g_aiCommitCounter (by 3 when the side is over its engagement budget, by 20 when missile troops fall under an eighth of the army) or makes the unit back away and call the missile units onto its attacker. It then charges any enemy unit of three or more figures within eight cells, and otherwise returns to rally waypoint 2 every fifth think.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldMelee
functions.comment: Field battle, unit categories 3 (macemen, swordsmen) and 4 (knights): both dispatch slots hold this one function. Identical in shape to UnitOrder_FieldFoot, with thirteen marching thinks rather than ten, a nine-cell charge radius rather than eight, a rally every eighth think, and a limit of two withdrawals per unit.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttMissile
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 1. Field corner on think 0, a castle approach point every fifteenth think, and from think 11 an alternation of two staging routines on an eleven-of-sixteen rotation. Once there is a breach it shoots into it, or moves onto the castle objective when it cannot.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttFoot
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 2. The longest of the order scripts: a ladder of `orders` thresholds (8, 18, 25, 31, 40, 51, 60, 71) alternating two staging positions, with a jump that sets `orders` to 100 when the castle layout flag is set. Charges outright once g_aiStrengthAdvantage reaches 151.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttMelee
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 3. The same staging ladder as UnitOrder_SiegeAttFoot with different thresholds (15, 25, 30, 41, 50, 61, 70, 81), plus a six-phase rotation deciding when to move onto the castle objective and when to hold.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttKnight
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 4. Moves to a field corner for ten thinks then cycles castle approach points until think 31. Also the only handler that raises the flag at 0x0056D5C8 - when the AI side is all knights and nothing is breached yet.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttCatapult
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 5 (catapults). Nothing for four thinks, a field corner to think 13, a castle approach to think 21, then from think 31 the nearest surface-4 cell within twenty cells of one of its figures - twenty cells being exactly the catapult firing range in g_missileStats. Has no in-melee gate, so it keeps thinking while engaged.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttTower
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 6 (siege towers). Moves to a field corner for eleven thinks, then - once g_siegeApproachScore passes 6 after think 60, or passes 10 at any time - widens a search from radius 10 to 30 for a surface-4 cell and moves onto it. This is the code that walks a tower up to the wall.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttRam
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 7 (battering rams). Ignores `orders` entirely: it picks between its stored secondary destination and a castle approach point from three flags - the castle layout flag, g_siegeApproachScore, and whether the drawbridge patch has been laid.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefMissile
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 1. Rotates through nine wall slots every other think while fewer than three attackers stand on the wall, and falls back on the castle objective when more do. Its sortie branch above g_aiSortieThreshold discards the Enemy_NearestUnit result and then calls Order_HalfwayToUnit on its own unit index, so it does nothing at all - see docs/battle-ai.md 6.3.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefFoot
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 2. Thinks every 100 frames rather than 200 and does not check the in-melee flag, so it keeps re-deciding while fighting. Its Enemy_NearestUnit(unit, 10, 0) call discards the result. Then either charges (sortie) or holds the castle objective.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefMelee
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 3. Thinks every 100 frames. Reserves a defence post with Siege_ClaimDefencePost, moves onto an attacking unit that has reached the wall, and otherwise rotates four inner wall slots every fifteenth think - abandoning all of it for the castle objective once four or more attackers are on the wall.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefKnight
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 4. Sits on wall-slot group 2 every twentieth think until a single attacker reaches the wall, then falls back on the castle objective. The most passive of the defender handlers.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefOil
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 8 (boiling oil). Calls Oil_FindPourTarget: if the unit is high enough on the wall it moves to the densest cluster of enemy figures within six cells (four if it is on the rampart proper), needing three enemies (two). Otherwise it retreats toward the keep.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefWallMissileA
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 9 - which BattleUnit_Create gives to the first missile unit raised for a side-0 siege defender. The handler does nothing but count its `orders` field up, so this unit holds the wall slot it was deployed on for the whole battle.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefWallMissileB
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 10 - the second missile unit of a side-0 siege defender. Moves to a wall cell beside the enemy figure its own men would rather not shoot at, and falls back on the wall below the keep once attackers reach the rampart.

functions.name: Enemy_NearestUnit
functions.signature: int Enemy_NearestUnit(int unit, int maxDist, int minFigures)
functions.comment: Unit-level target selection: the nearest enemy unit by Chebyshev distance between the two units' centres, within maxDist cells and holding at least minFigures figures; 0 if there is none. Missile units call it with maxDist 80 - the whole field - and melee units with 8 or 9.

functions.name: Melee_ChooseChaseTarget
functions.comment: Figure-level target selection for state 8, and the most visible AI decision in the game. Score is the Chebyshev distance to the enemy figure, halved if that figure carries a missile weapon, plus that figure's `targeted` counter; lowest wins. Siege engines and dead figures are skipped, there is no range limit, and the winner's `targeted` is raised by 2 so the next chaser picks somebody else.

functions.name: Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Missile_FindTarget with two extra weights: an enemy in state 9 (filling the moat) scores a quarter of its distance, and an enemy carrying a missile weapon scores half. Used by Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget to post defenders opposite the enemy shooters.

functions.name: Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: The mirror of Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters: state 9 still scores a quarter, but an enemy with a missile weapon scores double, so it is picked last. Used by Order_ToWallNearAvoidedTarget.

functions.name: Enemy_FindCluster
functions.signature: int Enemy_FindCluster(int x, int y, uint owner, int maxSurface, int radius, int minCount)
functions.comment: Counts live enemy figures on cells of surface <= maxSurface in a square of the given radius and returns the first such cell's byte offset, or 0 if fewer than minCount were found. The boiling-oil unit's aiming routine.

functions.name: Siege_FindCellSurface4
functions.signature: int Siege_FindCellSurface4(int x, int y, int radius, int maxElevation)
functions.comment: Nearest cell of surface 4 within a square radius whose elevation is at most maxElevation, left in g_foundWallX / g_foundWallY. Distance is Manhattan when maxElevation is 4 and min(|dx|,|dy|) otherwise. How catapults, siege towers and the wall-bound defenders find the wall.

functions.name: Siege_FindCellSurface5
functions.signature: bool Siege_FindCellSurface5(int x, int y, int radius)
functions.comment: Nearest cell of surface 5 within a square radius by Manhattan distance, left in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Used to put a defending unit on the rampart beside a given cell.

functions.name: BattleUnit_NeedsReform
functions.comment: Gate on the every-500-frame reform in Battle_UpdateAllUnits: false for an empty unit, for one whose byte +0x2A (halted) is set, and for a human-controlled unit of fewer than four figures that is not in melee. Its result also picks which slot-assignment pass BattleUnit_Reform runs.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Reform
functions.comment: Re-issues every figure of a unit a destination. If the formation rectangle around the unit's target is clear it assigns rectangle slots directly; if not it searches outward for free ground per figure; a siege tower past a siege-progress threshold sends every figure to the unit target instead. Clears the in-melee flag +0x13 afterwards.

functions.name: Formation_RectIsClear
functions.comment: Tests every slot of the unit's formation rectangle for being on the map, at the destination's elevation, free of another unit's figure and not impassable. Also caches the destination cell's occupant, its is-water flag and its elevation in the three globals the slot assignment then reads.

functions.name: Formation_AssignSearchedSlots
functions.comment: Slot assignment for a blocked destination: for each figure, search outward from the unit target for a usable cell, then send the nearest unassigned figure to it. Claimed cells go in a 100-entry list so two figures never get the same one.

functions.name: Formation_AssignRectSlots
functions.comment: Slot assignment for a clear destination: walk the formation rectangle in order and send the nearest unassigned figure to each slot. Greedy nearest-first, so the unit does not fold through itself.

functions.name: Formation_AssignAllToTarget
functions.comment: Slot assignment that sends every figure to the unit's target cell rather than to a rectangle. Used for a siege tower once g_siegeApproachScore passes 6.

functions.name: Formation_NearestFreeFigure
functions.signature: int Formation_NearestFreeFigure(int x, int y, int unit)
functions.comment: The live figure of `unit` nearest (x,y) by Manhattan distance that has not yet been given a slot in this pass, marked by figure byte +0x17C.

functions.name: Formation_SendFigure
functions.signature: void Formation_SendFigure(int x, int y, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Gives one figure its destination and entry state: 3 walk, 9 fill in the moat when the destination is water, 10 for a siege engine, 17 closing to attack when the figure has a bow or crossbow and something stands on the destination, 12 when a catapult is aimed at low ground. Clears the route and the barred counter if the destination changed.

functions.name: Formation_ComputeRect
functions.comment: Works out the unit's formation rectangle - columns, footprint, width, depth - and its top-left origin, centred on the unit target and clamped to the map. Forces the column count to 2 for units whose byte +0x09 is 1.

functions.name: Formation_FindNearbySlot
functions.comment: Expanding-ring search of radius 0..19 around the unit target for a cell Formation_SlotIsUsable accepts and that no figure of this pass has claimed. Short-circuits to the target itself on water, and on surface 4 for a catapult unit.

functions.name: Formation_SlotIsUsable
functions.signature: int Formation_SlotIsUsable(int cellOffset, uint surface, int elevation, int unit)
functions.comment: Whether one cell may serve as a formation slot: rejects an impassable cell that is also empty, accepts one holding an enemy figure, rejects one holding another friendly unit's figure, and in a siege refuses to put a side-0 unit on an empty low-surface cell.

functions.name: Formation_PickGeometry
functions.comment: Chooses which of the unit's troop types dictates the formation by taking the highest g_formationTypePriority, then loads that type's cell footprint and figures-per-row out of g_troopBattleStats.

functions.name: Order_DoNothing
functions.comment: An immediate return, called from the opening `orders` phases of the field handlers: the units stand still while the battle starts.

functions.name: Order_HoldPosition
functions.comment: Sets the unit's destination to its own current position and re-issues the order, stopping the unit where it stands and reforming it there.

functions.name: Order_ToSecondTarget
functions.comment: Copies the unit's second destination pair (+0x26/+0x28) into the live destination and re-issues the order. The battering ram's default move.

functions.name: Order_StepAwayFromUnit
functions.comment: Shifts the current unit's destination two cells directly away from `unit`, along the longer axis and along both when an axis separation exceeds five. Sets the withdrawing flag +0x10 and counts the withdrawal in +0x2B. This is the whole of the AI's retreat behaviour.

functions.name: Order_StepTowardRallyPoint
functions.comment: The mirror of Order_StepAwayFromUnit: shifts the destination two cells toward g_aiRallyX / g_aiRallyY and clears g_aiRallyRequest. How a missile unit answers a melee unit that has just been attacked.

functions.name: Order_ToRallyWaypoint
functions.comment: Moves the unit to one of three rally waypoints for its side, from g_rallyWaypoints indexed by g_battleRallyGroup. Both field battlefield builders fill that table; a .skr map puts all three on the deployment marker.

functions.name: Order_ToWallSlot
functions.comment: Moves a siege defender onto one of sixteen wall positions in one of the groups at 0x00554180, skipping empty entries and wrapping, offset one cell west and two north of the recorded position.

functions.name: Order_ToCastleApproach
functions.comment: Moves a siege attacker to one of four approach points per index from the castle layout tables at 0x0055CD90, selected by g_battleApproachLane. Rams always use the primary table; everyone else switches on the castle orientation flag.

functions.name: Order_ToFieldCorner
functions.comment: Sends a siege attacker to a fixed corner of the field - (6,74) or (74,74) - by castle layout, or to Order_ToCastleApproach when the layout flag is neither 1 nor 2. The opening move of most siege-attacker scripts.

functions.name: Order_ToCastleObjective
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto one of the two castle cells Battlefield_BuildCastle recorded: always the primary for mode 1, otherwise the secondary unless the moat flag or the castle index says otherwise.

functions.name: Order_ToWallBelowKeep
functions.comment: Takes the primary castle cell, drops four cells south, and moves onto the nearest surface-4 cell within five. The siege defender's fall-back position.

functions.name: Order_ToKeep
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto the secondary castle cell, offset two west and one north, when there is one; onto the primary when there is not.

functions.name: Order_ToCell
functions.comment: Converts a battlefield cell byte offset back into x,y and issues the move. The common tail of most siege order actions.

functions.name: Order_ToSurface5Near
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto the nearest surface-5 cell within five cells of the given cell, or does nothing if there is none.

functions.name: Order_OntoUnit
functions.comment: Sets the destination to another unit's position and issues the move: walk straight at the enemy. The melee handlers' aggressive answer to being hit.

functions.name: Order_HalfwayToUnit
functions.comment: Advances half the separation toward another unit. It does nothing at all unless one axis is separated by eight cells or more, and then shifts only those axes separated by six or more. This is why AI missile units advance in stages and then stop.

functions.name: Order_ChargeNearest
functions.comment: Sets the halted flag +0x2A and puts every figure of the unit into state 8 - free pursuit of the nearest enemy figure via Melee_ChooseChaseTarget - clearing their routes. The AI's all-out charge, and the only thing a siege defender does once it is overwhelmingly stronger.

functions.name: Order_ShootAtUnit
functions.comment: For each figure of the current unit, finds a target within forty cells restricted to `unit` and puts the figure into state 17 aimed at it. Returns 0 if any figure found nothing, which the caller reads as "that unit is out of reach".

functions.name: Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget
functions.comment: Picks a target with Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters, then moves the unit onto the nearest surface-4 cell within twenty of that target.

functions.name: Order_ToWallNearAvoidedTarget
functions.comment: As Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget but choosing with Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters, so the unit posts itself opposite enemy foot rather than enemy shooters.

functions.name: Order_ToNearestWallCell
functions.comment: Moves onto the nearest surface-4 cell within forty cells of the unit, or does nothing if there is none.

functions.name: Order_ToBreachOrStaging
functions.comment: While g_siegeApproachScore is under 16 it searches radii 12..19 for a way in and moves there; between 16 and 400 it falls back on the secondary staging table; above 400 it does nothing at all.

functions.name: Order_ToSiegeStaging
functions.comment: The siege attacker's staging move: the primary approach table when g_siegeApproachScore is below 16 or above 399, the secondary table five cells further in between, or a fixed offset from the castle when the orientation flag is set.

functions.name: Oil_FindPourTarget
functions.comment: The cell a boiling-oil unit should move to: nothing when its own cell is below elevation 2; otherwise the densest enemy cluster within six cells needing three enemies (own surface below 6), or within four needing two (surface 6 and above).

functions.name: Oil_IsOnHighWall
functions.comment: True when the unit stands at elevation 2 or more on a cell of surface 6 or above. Decides whether an oil unit holds its post or falls back.

functions.name: BattleUnit_FewOnRampart
functions.comment: True when fewer than four of the unit's live figures stand on cells of surface 4 or above, and only once the drawbridge patch has been laid.

functions.name: Siege_ClaimDefencePost
functions.comment: A twenty-entry (cell, unit) reservation table. Returns the cell already reserved for this unit, or reserves the first free non-empty entry for it. Stops two defending units posting to the same place.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateWalk
functions.comment: Figure state 3: walk toward tg x / tg y and drop to state 5 (idle) when the mover reports an interruption. The state Formation_SendFigure uses for an ordinary move.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateChase
functions.comment: Figure state 8: free pursuit. Re-acquires a target with Melee_ChooseChaseTarget whenever it has none or its target is dead, copies the target's position into its own tg x / tg y every tick, and walks. Siege engines are bounced to state 11 instead. This state ignores the unit's destination entirely.

functions.name: Path_BuildTerrainTemplate
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_pathBlockedTemplate, the cost field Path_Search copies at the start of every search: 999 for a cell whose flags carry 0x10 or 0x40 and for the one-cell border, 0 everywhere else. It ignores flags 0x80 and 0x20, both of which Cell_TryEnter treats as blocking, so the pathfinder's map is more permissive than the mover's.

functions.name: Path_BuildElevation
functions.comment: Copies cell byte +4 of all 6,400 battlefield cells into g_pathElevation.

functions.name: Path_BuildStepCost
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_pathStepCost, and is the pathfinder's entire cost function. Zero everywhere except: a cell whose flags carry 0x20 or 0x40 costs 100 and lays a gradient of 12, 8, 4, 4 on the cells one to four rows further south (three cells wide in the last two bands); and, when the flag at 0x0057C910 is set, a cell diagonally adjacent to surface 5 costs 4. Battlefield_BuildFromSkr sets neither 0x20 nor 0x40, so on a .skr battlefield every step costs the same.

functions.name: Path_NearestReachedNear
functions.signature: int Path_NearestReachedNear(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The salvage step after Path_Extract fails: an expanding-ring search of radius 0..29 around the unreachable destination for the cheapest cell the flood fill actually reached at the destination's elevation, left in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Gives up if the ring reaches the figure's own position.

functions.name: Path_DetourTooLong
functions.comment: Cancels a move whose route is absurd: true when the path cost to the destination exceeds 20 in a field battle or 150 in a siege and is also more than five times the straight-line Chebyshev distance. It can only ever return true for a figure whose owner is human, so a player's men give up on long detours and the AI's never do.

functions.name: Rand_Advance
functions.comment: The pseudo-random generator the battle AI uses. Two 31-bit Fibonacci LFSRs (taps at bits 0 and 4) are each stepped 31 times, then masked into six output globals - &0x7FFF, &0x7F and &7 per generator. Distinct from FUN_00404B2C / DAT_005C9A84, the counter the battlefield builders use.

functions.name: Dist_MinAxis
functions.signature: int Dist_MinAxis(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns min(|dx|, |dy|) and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy. The third member of the Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev family; used by Siege_FindCellSurface4.

functions.name: Battle_Frame
functions.comment: The battle frame loop. Calls Battle_CountMenByType, Battle_UpdateAllMen, Missile_UpdateAll, BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures, Battle_UpdateAllUnits and BattleDebug_Panel, which fixes all of them at once per frame - and so fixes the unit timers those passes age.

globals.name: g_clipState
globals.comment: Clip state: 0 unclipped, 1 clipped left, 2 clipped right, 5 fully offscreen.

globals.name: g_clipVisibleWidth
globals.comment: Visible (clipped) sprite width.

globals.name: g_clipSrcSkip
globals.comment: Source bytes skipped per row = width - visible width.

globals.name: g_clipDstAdvance
globals.comment: Destination advance per row = screen stride - visible width.

globals.name: g_spriteWidth
globals.comment: Current sprite width.

globals.name: g_spriteHeight
globals.comment: Current sprite height.

globals.name: g_spriteDataOffset
globals.comment: Current source data offset within the PL8 buffer.

globals.name: g_screenStride
globals.comment: Screen stride, 640.

globals.name: g_blitRowCount
globals.comment: Blitter row counter. Not frame-record byte 0x0D - Clip_Vertical overwrites it before every blit, so the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

globals.name: g_ddrawInterface
globals.comment: A DirectDraw interface pointer. It was NULL at the crash at 0x004522B5, which happened when the window was deactivated during startup under DxWnd.

globals.name: g_resourceTable
globals.comment: The game's resource directory: {char name[16]; u32 size;} records. Entries 0-31 are the map tile sets, eight layers x four seasons; 32-63 the zoom-2 sets; 64+ the battle-map sets. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 1.1.

globals.name: g_scenarioIndex
globals.comment: Current scenario. Its low 2 bits select the season variant of the tile set; the rest selects the map slot and the MAPnn.PL8 file.

globals.name: g_tiles
globals.comment: Runtime tile array, 4096 records x 8 bytes, index y*64 + x. +1 plane0 flags, +2 bank, +3 frame, +4 plane3, +5 unit index on this tile, +6 saved terrain frame, +7 county. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.3.

globals.name: g_screenLattice
globals.comment: Runtime 129x65 dword screen lattice, row stride 0x104. Covered cells hold tileIndex*8; uncovered cells keep 0x0FFF0000 + backgroundFrame.

globals.name: g_countyCount
globals.comment: Highest county id on the loaded map, i.e. the county count. Set by Map_LoadPlanes as max(plane5) over ids below 0x11.

globals.name: g_units
globals.comment: Unit array, 150 records x 0x1A4 bytes, index 1..149 (0 unused). +0x00 owner, +0x08 type, +0x0A/+0x0B tile x/y, +0x0C tile offset, +0x10 county, +0x14..+0x17 destination x/y, +0x14F merchant route index, +0x150 'needs a destination', +0x151 destination county, +0x164 merchant route cursor, +0x16C.. cargo.

globals.name: g_lastUnitIndex
globals.comment: Index of the unit Unit_Spawn just allocated. Callers read it straight after the call to fill in the rest of the record.

globals.name: g_foundTileX
globals.comment: X of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_foundTileY
globals.comment: Y of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_merchantRoutes
globals.comment: The six merchant trade routes: 6 rows x 16 county ids, built from plane 4 on castle tiles. Row n is the itinerary of the merchant named by L2.eng group 5 string n. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

globals.name: g_merchantStartCounty
globals.comment: Six bytes: the county each merchant starts in, chosen by Merchant_PickStartCounties. A zero entry stops Merchant_SpawnAll.

globals.name: g_merchantCount
globals.comment: Number of merchants Merchant_SpawnAll actually placed, 1..6.

globals.name: g_playerStartTable
globals.comment: Player start table, {county, slot} byte pairs indexed by the plane-4 value on a settlement tile. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

globals.name: g_playerStartCount
globals.comment: Number of non-zero player start slots on the loaded map: 5, 4 or 2 across the shipped maps.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorX
globals.comment: X of county 0's anchor tile in the county record array (stride 0x300); County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around county*0x300 + this.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorY
globals.comment: Y of county 0's anchor tile, as above.

globals.name: g_turnPhase
globals.comment: Turn state machine phase, switched on by FUN_0049a010. Phase 6 step 1 is Merchant_AdvanceAll.

globals.name: g_turnPhaseStep
globals.comment: Step counter within the current turn phase; incremented on every FUN_0049a010 call.

globals.name: g_battleMen
globals.comment: Battle figure array, 80 records of 0x1B0 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A figure is one drawn man representing g_menPerFigure real soldiers. +0x09 selected, +0x12 troop type, +0x13 owner is human, +0x18 facing 0..7, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x20/+0x22 x,y, +0x24/+0x26 target x,y, +0x2C owner (0 = free slot), +0x31 state, +0x172 armour, +0x174 target figure, +0x178 owning unit, +0x17A side, +0x17E melee opponent, +0x189 move delay, +0x18B melee recovery interval, +0x197 strength band, +0x198 heavy-blow bonus, +0x19A hits, +0x19C melee attack, +0x1A0 men left. Full map in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_battleUnits
globals.comment: Battle unit array, 80 records of 0x34 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A unit is what the player selects and orders. +0x00 owner (0 = free slot), +0x01 human controlled, +0x02 figure count, +0x03 side (0 or 4), +0x04/+0x06 first and last figure index, +0x08 category, +0x0F firing timer, +0x14 re-target countdown, +0x1A orders, +0x1E/+0x20 position, +0x22/+0x24 target, +0x2C ordered target figure, +0x30 target cell offset.

globals.name: g_missiles
globals.comment: Missile / effect array, 100 records of 0x4C bytes, index 1..100. +0x06 firing figure, +0x08 owner, +0x09 class (1 bow, 2 crossbow, 3 catapult, 5 fire, 7 falling figure), +0x0A/+0x0C position in 1/32 cell, +0x14/+0x16 cell x,y, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x2F launch elevation, +0x36 distance flown, +0x38 range, +0x40 power.

globals.name: g_battlefield
globals.comment: Battlefield cell array, 80x80 records of 8 bytes, index (y*80 + x)*8. +0 terrain id, +1 flags (0x10 and 0x80 impassable), +2 flags, +3 graphic index, +4 elevation, +5 index of the figure standing here, +6 head of the missile list in this cell, +7 surface type (7 bridge, 10 and 17 burning, 15 woodland).

globals.name: g_curBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure currently being updated. The whole figure state machine reads its subject from this global rather than from a parameter.

globals.name: g_otherBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the other figure in the current interaction: the melee opponent, the missile target, or the figure being swapped with.

globals.name: g_curBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit currently being updated by Battle_UpdateAllUnits.

globals.name: g_lastBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure BattleMan_Create just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit BattleUnit_Alloc just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Spawn just allocated.

globals.name: g_curMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Step is advancing.

globals.name: g_battleSizeClass
globals.comment: Battlefield size class 0..8, from the combined army size. It selects g_menPerFigure, the strength-band thresholds, and the burning-damage rate.

globals.name: g_menPerFigure
globals.comment: How many real soldiers one drawn figure stands for: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 by size class. Reduced for a small army so that a side always gets at least 9 figures.

globals.name: g_battleIsSiege
globals.comment: Non-zero for a siege: selects the castle battlefield builder, the siege unit-order tables and Battle_RaiseSideSiege.

globals.name: g_localPlayer
globals.comment: The player index this machine controls. Compared against a unit owner to decide whose units are on the player side.

globals.name: g_strengthBand1
globals.comment: Men in a figure below which it drops to strength band 1 - 75% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand2
globals.comment: Band 2 threshold - 50% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand3
globals.comment: Band 3 threshold - about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_absDx
globals.comment: Absolute x distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_absDy
globals.comment: Absolute y distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_troopStrengthWeight
globals.comment: Seven ints, the autocalc strength weight of one soldier by troop type: peasant 2, crossbowman 16, maceman 8, swordsman 13, pikeman 9, archer 13, knight 22. Used only for army strength comparisons, not by the real-time battle.

globals.name: g_troopBattleStats
globals.comment: Per troop type, 11 rows of 5 ints: max figures per unit, cell footprint, max figures per formation row, weapon class (index into g_missileStats), move delay in ticks.

globals.name: g_missileStats
globals.comment: Per weapon class, 4 rows of 5 ints: range in 1/8 cells, reload interval in ticks, sub-steps per tick, damage, sprite-bank offset. Class 0 melee (all zero), 1 bow (120, 50, 4, 50, 0), 2 crossbow (64, 100, 4, 200, 8), 3 catapult (160, 100, 4, 200, 16).

globals.name: g_meleeAttackTable
globals.comment: Melee attack value by troop type and strength band, 11 rows of 4 shorts. Peasant/crossbow/archer 5,4,3,2; mace and sword 15,12,10,6; pike 10,8,6,5; knight 20,15,11,6; siege engines all zero.

globals.name: g_menPerFigureTable
globals.comment: Nine ints indexed by battlefield size class: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 men per drawn figure.

globals.name: g_sizeClassLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, size class) pairs mapping total men to the battlefield size class: 305, 609, 1217, 2433, 4865, 9729, 19457, 38913, then 8.

globals.name: g_siegeScaleLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, value) pairs giving how many men one siege engine counts as when choosing the size class.

globals.name: g_strengthBandTable
globals.comment: Three ints per battlefield size class: the men-per-figure thresholds for strength bands 1, 2 and 3 - 75%, 50% and about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_raiseOrder
globals.comment: The order in which troop types become units in a field battle: ram, oil, knight, sword, mace, pike, crossbow, archer, peasant, tower, catapult.

globals.name: g_raiseOrderSiege
globals.comment: The castle-defender raise order, eight troop types: oil, archer, crossbow, knight, peasant, sword, mace, pike. Catapults, towers and rams are absent.

globals.name: g_troopTickTable
globals.comment: Eleven function pointers indexed by troop type. Each reloads that troop per-tick constants - animation set, recovery interval, heavy-blow bonus, armour - and then tail-calls g_manStateTable[state].

globals.name: g_manStateTable
globals.comment: Eighteen figure-state handlers indexed by figure byte +0x31. Known: 2 dead, 4 melee, 5 idle/firing, 6 blocked, 7 look for melee, 12 siege engine attacking, 17 closing to attack.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableField
globals.comment: Five unit order handlers for a field battle, indexed by unit category 0..4.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeAtt
globals.comment: Nine unit order handlers for the siege attacker (unit side non-zero), indexed by unit category 0..8.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeDef
globals.comment: Eleven unit order handlers for the siege defender (unit side zero), indexed by unit category 0..10.

globals.name: g_cellNeighbourOffsets
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell byte offsets of the neighbours in direction order 0..7: -0x280, -0x278, +8, +0x288, +0x280, +0x278, -8, -0x288.

globals.name: g_troopsTable
globals.comment: The parsed TROOPS*.ENG table: short[35][2][5][11], row stride 0xDC, side stride 0x6E, difficulty stride 0x16. See docs/formats/eng.md and the correction in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_troopsAdvantage
globals.comment: The per-battle defensive advantage 0..10, one per TROOPS*.ENG row.

globals.name: g_troopsRowBase
globals.comment: Four ints, 0/10/20/35: the first g_troopsTable row for each battle category.

globals.name: g_battleArmyA
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the first army in the current battle. It is raised on side 4.

globals.name: g_battleArmyB
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the second army. It is raised on side 0, and is the side the castle-defender path is applied to in a siege.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthA
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army A: sum of count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over troop types 0..6.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthB
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army B.

globals.name: g_debugSelectedMan
globals.comment: The figure index BattleDebug_Panel prints.

globals.name: g_pathCost
globals.comment: Pathfinder cost field, u16 per battlefield cell, index y*80 + x. 0 means unvisited, 1 the start cell, 998 (0x3E6) blocked.

globals.name: g_pathQueue
globals.comment: Pathfinder frontier, a circular queue of 0x1900 cell indices with head g_pathQueueHead and tail g_pathQueueTail.

globals.name: g_pathQueueHead
globals.comment: Read cursor of g_pathQueue.

globals.name: g_pathQueueTail
globals.comment: Write cursor of g_pathQueue; wraps at 0x1900.

globals.name: g_pathStepCost
globals.comment: Per-cell step cost the flood fill charges: a cell is only expanded once it has been reached this many times.

globals.name: g_pathVisitCount
globals.comment: How many times the flood fill has reached each cell, compared against g_pathStepCost.

globals.name: g_pathElevation
globals.comment: Per-cell elevation the flood fill and Path_Extract read; a step is only allowed between cells differing by at most 1.

globals.name: g_pathWaypoints
globals.comment: Scratch route built by Path_Extract: (x, y) byte pairs, at most 150, ordered destination-first. BattleMan_SetPath copies it into the figure.

globals.name: g_cellIndexNeighbours
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell-index (not byte) deltas in direction order 0..7: -0x50, -0x4F, +1, +0x51, +0x50, +0x4F, -1, -0x51.

globals.name: g_counties
globals.comment: The county array: 17 records of 0x300 bytes, index 1..16 (0 unused). Base, count and stride all appear together in the multiplayer sync descriptor at 0x004D5B10 and in the save-block table at 0x004DE960.

globals.name: g_realms
globals.comment: Realm/player array: 6 records of 0x160 bytes, index 1..5. +0x00 AI step, +0x04 in play, +0x05 human, +0x07 lord, +0x28 empire tax happiness, +0x2B rank, +0x50 score, +0xFC army wages, +0x118 gold.

globals.name: g_countyFieldTiles
globals.comment: 17 x 20 u32 tile indices - the map tiles that are this county's farm fields. Save block 12 is exactly 1360 bytes = 17 * 80.

globals.name: g_saveBlocks
globals.comment: 225 {u32 address, u32 length} records terminated by a zero length; Save_Write dumps each in order. Sums to 267,028 bytes.

globals.name: g_syncBlocks
globals.comment: Seven 12-byte {count, stride, firstComparedOffset} descriptors used by Sync_CompareState and Sync_Checksum: counties (17, 0x300, 5), realms (6, 0x160, 6), units (151, 0x1A4, 0), battle men (81, 0x1B0, 18), missiles (101, 0x4C, 4), battle units (81, 0x34, 0).

globals.name: g_stateArrayPtrs
globals.comment: Eight pointers in the same order as g_syncBlocks: counties, counties, realms, units, battle men, missiles, battle units, battlefield. No reader was found; it corroborates every base address.

globals.name: g_season
globals.comment: Current season 1..4, used directly as the index into L2.eng group 29 (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). Season_Advance sets it before running the economy, so the economy sees the season being entered.

globals.name: g_seasonNext
globals.comment: The season after g_season; the year rolls when the season that just ended was 4.

globals.name: g_seasonPrev
globals.comment: The previous value of g_season.

globals.name: g_year
globals.comment: Displayed year. 1268 on turn 1.

globals.name: g_yearNext
globals.comment: g_year + 1, staged for the next roll.

globals.name: g_turnCount
globals.comment: Turns elapsed; divides the happiness accumulator to give the running average.

globals.name: g_selectedCounty
globals.comment: The county the county panels display.

globals.name: g_weatherCounty
globals.comment: The county picked this season for the doubled local weather swing.

globals.name: g_optDifficulty
globals.comment: New-game difficulty 0..3 (easy/normal/hard/impossible, L2.eng group 103 indices 11..14). Scales AI gold, AI free resources and AI army wages.

globals.name: g_optAdvancedFarming
globals.comment: Advanced Farming (L2.eng group 102 index 0). When 0, weather is forced to Cloudy in every county and fertility is forced to 0.

globals.name: g_optArmiesEat
globals.comment: Armies Eat (L2.eng group 102 index 3). When 1, garrison and enemy troop counts are added to the county's food requirement.

globals.name: g_optTimeLimit
globals.comment: Turn time limit in seconds, 0 for none.
